PRINCIPAL MACT, AT BANGALORE, ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING :
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-claimant, calling in question the judgment and award dated 08.07.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.3826/2014, on the file of the Member Principal Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) for seeking enhancement of the compensation.

Brief facts:
2. On 08.07.2014 at about 2.05 p.m., the claimant was crossing Hosur Road in front of Seasons Hotel, Electronic City Gate-1.
At that time, a lorry bearing No.KA- OS-4653 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner from Bengaluru side towards Hosur dashed the claimant.
As a result, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant- claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act,
claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Siva Shankaran K @ Shiva Shankar K vs M/S Icici Lombard Gen.Insurance Co.Ltd on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34116855/
2 Rs.2,87,840/-, along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.

entities.text: Siva Shankaran K @ Shiva Shankar K vs M/S Icici Lombard Gen.Insurance Co.Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 to 2 therein, jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and the learned counsel for respondent No.1 - insurance company and perused the materials on record.
5.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:
1. Pain and Sufferings : Rs. 35,000/-
2. Medical Expenses : Rs. 96,000/-
3. Conveyance Attendant : Rs. 10,000/-
Charges, Nourishing Food 4. Loss of Income during Laid Up : Rs. 21,000/-
period 5. Loss of Future Earning Capacity : Rs. 1,05,840/-
Due to Disability 6. Loss of Amenities : Rs. 20,000/-
TOTAL : Rs. 2,87,840/-
6.

It is seen from the medical evidence on record, viz., Exhibit-P6 which is Wound Certificate and Exhibit-P7 which is Discharge Report, that the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
"i. Severe Head Injury with left EDH and Fracture of left temporo parietal bone, ii.
Right hemispheric edema, iii. Bilateral minimal hemothorax"
7.
In the present case the claimant had suffered head injury including fracture of left temporal of bone.
The Doctor has assessed disability at 10% to the whole-body.
But the Tribunal has taken the physical disability at 7%, which is on lesser side.

The claimant is complaining of double vision,
difficulty in driving, slurred speech.
Therefore, just because PW-2 is not the treated Doctor that cannot be said that he is not certified to say regarding the disability.
PW-2 may be an Ortho-Surgeon, but upon seeing the patient what would be the disability would be assessed by any Medical Officer.
The criteria for calculating functional disability is elaborately discussed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore,
considering the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court (2011) 1 SCC 343 stated Siva Shankaran K @ Shiva Shankar K vs M/S Icici Lombard Gen.Insurance Co.Ltd on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34116855/
3 supra, and the injuries suffered by the appellant and the avocation of the appellant-claimant being Customer Service Associate - Voice at M/s.Serco B.P.O. Private Limited, certainly the disability will affect his earning capacity.

sentences.text: Accordingly, 10% functional disability to the whole-body as assessed by the Doctor is taken.
The claimant was aged 23 years and the accident has occurred during the year 2014.
The Tribunal has held the income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/- per month, which is on lesser side.
Therefore, as per Chart of notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, a sum of Rs.8,500/- is to be taken as notional monthly income of the claimant.
The appropriate multiplier applicable as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others.
Vs. Delhi Transport Corpn And Another2 is '18'.

Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss of Earning Capacity Due to Disability' is recalculated and quantified as follows:
AIR 2009 SC 3104 Rs.8,500/- x 10% x 18 x 12 = Rs.1,83,600/-
8.
The aforesaid injuries are grievous in nature.
Therefore, considering this, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'Pain and Sufferings, at Rs.35,000/-, is on lesser side and hence a sum of Rs.45,000/- is awarded.

9. The compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal under the 'Medical Expenses' at Rs.96,000/-
is as per actual bills and receipts and the same is kept in tact.
10. The Tribunal has awarded compensation towards 'Loss Of Amenities' at Rs.20,000/-, which is on lesser side and hence a sum of Rs.35,000/- is awarded under the said head.
11. In view of the accidental injuries, the claimant would have taken rest for atleast for a period of Three months.

Therefore, by taking income at Rs.8,500/- per month and calculating the laid up period for Three months, the claimant is entitled for a sum of Rs.25,500/- (Rs.8,500 x 3 months),
under the head 'Loss Of Earning During Laid Up Period'.

12. The Tribunal has awarded compensation towards 'Food, Nourishment, Conveyance and Attendant Charges' at Rs.10,000/-, which is on lesser side and hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the said head.

13. Therefore, in modification of the award of the Tribunal, the appellant-claimant is entitled to the following compensation:
1. Pain and Sufferings : Rs. 45,000/-
2. Medical Expenses : Rs. 96,000/-
3. Conveyance Attendant : Rs. 25,000/-
Charges, Nourishing Food Siva Shankaran K @ Shiva Shankar K vs M/S Icici Lombard Gen.Insurance Co.Ltd on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34116855/
4 4. Loss of Income during Laid Up : Rs. 25,500/-
period (Rs.8,500 x 3 months)
5. Loss of Future Earning Capacity : Rs. 1,83,600/-
Due to Disability Rs.8,500/- x 10% x 18 x 12 6. Loss of Amenities : Rs. 35,000/-
TOTAL : Rs. 4,10,100/-
14.
Therefore, the appellant-claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,10,100/- as against Rs.2,87,840/-.

The appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.1,22,260/-
(Rs.4,10,100 - Rs.2,87,840) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of total compensation within Eight Weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.

15. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is Allowed In Part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 08.07.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.3826/2014, on - 10 - the file of the Member Principal Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru is modified to the aforesaid extent.
